relevant_laws.name: Article 206 of the French Tax Code
relevant_laws.description: This article can subject a civil company (SCI) renting furnished premises to corporate income tax if the furnished activity is considered commercial and not genuinely ancillary.

key_facts: The LMNP (Loueur en Meublé Non Professionnel) status is an individual investment, whereas an SCI (Société Civile Immobilière) is a collective investment.

Under the IR (Impôt sur le Revenu) regime for an SCI, each partner is taxed individually on their share of the gain as if they owned the property directly. The tax rate is 19% for income tax plus 17.2% for social charges. Over time, these taxes are reduced, leading to full exemption from income tax after 22 years and social charges after 30 years.

An SCI can rent furnished property, but if the furnished activity is not ancillary or remains within tolerated limits, it may be subject to corporate income tax under article 206 of the French Tax Code.
The sale of a property under LMNP can generate a professional gain taxed differently from classic real estate gains.
An SCI offers flexibility in real estate administration, potentially allowing for the combination of collective management profits with advantageous taxation and optimized property transmission.
LMNP advantages include tax benefits such as reductions on income tax (IR) and the possibility of deducting rental charges and depreciation.
LMNP allows for the depreciation of the property and furniture, significantly reducing social levies. VAT recovery is also a major advantage for new acquisitions.

Inconveniences of LMNP include a profit limitation of €23,000 per year, the inclusion of rented properties in the calculation of IFI (Impôt sur la Fortune Immobilière), and the need for annual accounting and a profit and loss statement, often requiring an accountant.
An SCI, when subject to corporate income tax (IS), can lead to double taxation: IS (15-25%) and then a 30% PFU (Prélèvement Forfaitaire Unique) on dividends.

A SARL de famille (family LLC) that opts for IR can combine LMNP advantages (depreciation of BIC - Bénéfices Industriels et Commerciaux) with those of a company, such as part transmission, splitting, and limited liability. The IR option is unlimited in time as long as family ties are maintained.
